AMP NIN - Inpatient Cardiology Progress Note
Salient Cardiac Features


77-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, coronary artery disease with extensive coronary calcification, pulmonary hypertension, and dysautonomia with significant orthostatic hypotension and labile hypertension.


Hospitalization complicated by substantial blood pressure fluctuations, including significant blood pressure decline with standing.


Family has been educated regarding dysautonomia, orthostatic hypotension, and the previously discussed permissive supine systolic blood pressure goal of approximately 180 mmHg.


Formal tilt-table testing has not yet been performed and may be considered if clinically necessary.


Continues Eliquis for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.


Recent nuclear stress testing was negative for ischemia.


From a cardiovascular standpoint, patient may discharge home if otherwise clinically appropriate and sufficiently strong for safe discharge.


SOAP Note
Subjective
Seen during inpatient cardiology rounds. Hospital course and ongoing blood pressure fluctuations were reviewed. Patient has known dysautonomia with significant orthostatic hypotension and labile hypertension.
Family has been educated regarding the significant decline in blood pressure with standing and the previously discussed strategy of tolerating a higher supine blood pressure, with a goal around 180 mmHg. Continued education was provided regarding the chronic and difficult-to-control nature of dysautonomia.
Patient has been compliant with outpatient follow-up through the office chronic care management concierge program.
Objective
Vitals reviewed elsewhere.
General: Clinically stable without acute distress.
Cardiovascular: Significant blood pressure lability with known orthostatic hypotension and episodic supine hypertension.
Respiratory: No acute respiratory distress.
Neurologic: Intermittent dizziness in the setting of dysautonomia and orthostatic hypotension. No new focal neurologic changes documented.
Abdomen: No acute abdominal findings documented.
Extremities: No distal pitting edema documented.
Laboratory data reviewed. Sodium 132 mmol/L, potassium 4.4 mmol/L, creatinine 1.01 mg/dL. Recent nuclear stress study was negative for ischemia. Formal tilt-table testing has not yet been performed.
Assessment


Dysautonomia with significant orthostatic hypotension and labile/supine hypertension (ICD-10: G90.1, I95.1, R09.89)


Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (ICD-10: I48.0)


Coronary artery disease (ICD-10: I25.10)


Pulmonary hypertension (ICD-10: I27.20)


Chest pain, status post negative nuclear ischemic evaluation (ICD-10: R07.9)


Chronic hyponatremia (ICD-10: E87.1)


History of mesenteric ischemia status post SMA thrombectomy (ICD-10: K55.9)


Plan


High-complexity inpatient medical decision-making performed due to significant dysautonomia with marked orthostatic blood pressure changes and labile hypertension requiring individualized blood pressure targets, medication management, fall-risk assessment, and extensive patient/family counseling.


Continue conservative management of dysautonomia and orthostatic hypotension.


Family educated that significant blood pressure decline with standing is expected with her underlying dysautonomia and that overly aggressive treatment of supine hypertension may exacerbate symptomatic orthostatic hypotension.


Continue previously discussed permissive supine systolic blood pressure goal around 180 mmHg.


Formal tilt-table testing has not yet been performed and may be considered if additional diagnostic clarification is clinically necessary.


Continue Eliquis and current atrial fibrillation management.


Continue close monitoring for symptomatic hypotension, severe hypertension, syncope/presyncope, or clinically significant arrhythmia.


Patient is enrolled in our office chronic care management concierge program and has remained compliant with follow-up.


From a cardiology standpoint, patient should be able to discharge home if otherwise clinically appropriate and sufficiently strong for safe discharge.


If safe disposition remains problematic, consider goals-of-care discussion with the patient and family.


Office staff to arrange transitional care management with follow-up within 5 working days/7 total days.


Nursing Communication


Continue telemetry monitoring while hospitalized.


Obtain and document orthostatic blood pressures.


Use fall precautions and assist with standing and ambulation because of significant orthostatic hypotension.


Avoid reacting to isolated elevated supine blood pressure without considering the patient's known dysautonomia and substantial standing blood pressure decline.


Notify the treating team for syncope/presyncope, symptomatic hypotension, sustained severe hypertension outside established parameters, recurrent chest pain, significant arrhythmia, or other acute deterioration.


Continue PT/OT and mobilization as tolerated to assess readiness for safe discharge.
